newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta shares ends up but off early highs.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta shares ends up but off early highs.

text.p: Jakarta shares ended up on Thursday but were off earlier highs as some investors took profit in selected big and medium-sized stocks, brokers said.
The Jakarta Composite Index rose 7.25 points, or 1.24 percent, to close at 594.59 points after hitting a high of 598.07 points. Gainers led losers by 77 to 36, while 52 counters were unchanged.

Brokers said the market was likely to continue being active on Friday as possibly more investors return to the market due to end of the four-day public offer period by Bank Negara Indonesia (BNI) on Thursday.
After five consecutive days of gains, there's likely to be some profit taking tomorrow, they said.
But brokers said they believe the index was likely to remain in positive territory at the early session on Friday as market sentiment remained firm.
Overall trading today, brokers said, was dominated by foreigners as most locals concentrated on the BNI offer.

The bank is floating 1.085 billion shares at a price of 850 rupiah each ahead of its November 25 listing on the Jakarta and Surabaya exchanges. The BNI offer had slowed trading the past two weeks as many investors eyed the stock, brokers said. "It was well-received in Jakarta and had improved sentiment on other bank issues," said one broker.
Brokers said secondaries including Bank BDNI, Bank Danamon, Bank International Indonesia, Modern Bank drew investors.
"Some investors are just using the momentum to speculate," an analyst with a local securities said.
Bank BDNI topped the active list with 13.3 million shares traded, rising 150 rupiah to 1,975 on what brokers said was due to its fundamentals coupled with speculative interest.

Heavyweight Telkom rose 50 rupiah to 3,850 on a turnover of about seven million shares. Brokers said it was due to its high closing price in New York overnight coupled with talk that some investors were switching from Indosat to Telkom.

"Some investors were selling off Indosat on the perception that its nine-month results were slightly below expectations," said one foreign analyst. It fell 3.07 percent from 7,325 rupiah on a turnover of 1.1 million shares.
On Wednesday, Indosat reported a nine-month net income of 361.6 billion rupiah, compared with 342.9 billion rupiah in the same 1995 period.

Blue-chip Semen Gresik rose 600 rupiah to 7,600 on a volume of 1.6 million shares. It had earlier touched 7,725 rupiah. Brokers attributed the increase to foreign buying on its fundamentals and opinion that its price was fairly stable.
Brokers said toll road operator Citra Marga and conglomerate Bimantara Citra were among actively-traded stocks targeted by foreigners.
Toll road operator Citra Marga traded unchanged at 1,900 rupiah after hitting a high of 2,100 rupiah, with 6.7 million shares changing hands.
"I recommend a 'buy' for Citra Marga, it has good fundamentals," one foreign analyst said.
